glance.question: Is AI a tool to use, a force to resist, or a frontier to shape?

positions.name: Resist and Limit
positions.claim: AI forms us; keep it out of preaching, writing, friendship and worship.

positions.name: Use With Guardrails
positions.claim: A common grace tool: use it, but keep it servant, not master.

positions.name: Shape It for the Mission
positions.claim: Christians must build and use AI well, or others will shape it.

positions.name: Human Dignity First
positions.claim: The real question is what a human is, not what machines can do.

start_here.title: How Should Christians Think About AI?
start_here.author: Samuel D. James
start_here.why: A short, measured way in: weigh AI by what Scripture says about work, creativity and relationship.

start_here.title: Using AI Wisely: A Pastor’s Encouragement to His Church
start_here.author: Aaron Menikoff
start_here.why: Ten questions a pastor gave his own congregation to ask before they use AI.

start_here.title: What Is a Human in the AI Age?
start_here.author: Chris Watkin
start_here.why: Why the AI debate keeps returning to what a human being is.

key_number.text: One in 10 pastors (10%) say they are regular users of artificial intelligence, while a third (32%) are experimenting with it.
key_number.study: Pastors, Churchgoers See AI as Concerning and Confusing

changes.text: launched this page, replacing Artificial Intelligence and the Church, with four positions, survey charts, key documents, a FAQ and a glossary.

notes: Voices verified in their own words on Nov 14 2026: Moore (CT, 2025-11-12, body: 'Ultimately, we find that in disconnecting from real community and cleaving to our own prompts and algorithmically discerned preferences, we are all alone.'); Hansen (TGC, 2026-08-10: 'We’re not anti-tech. We’re pro-human. We refuse to surrender our minds to the machines.'); Williams (CT, 2026-04-09, body: 'Using AI to generate text is just such a disordered means.'); Kingsnorth (UnHerd interview, 2025-09-26: 'We’re trying to create God, make God live forever.'; Eastern Orthodox, labeled on the card only); Haidt and Rausch (After Babel, 2025-11-24: 'An AI companion can imitate friendship, but it can’t actually be a friend.'; secular, labeled on the card only); Challies (challies.com, 2026-03-18: 'For Christians, AI must remain a servant and never become a master.'); Menikoff (9Marks, 2026-07-24: 'I’m not exhorting you to avoid this technology; I’m simply encouraging you to use it well.'); Bahnsen (TGC, 2026-05-18: 'Our task isn’t to reject technology or baptize it uncritically but to approach it with hopeful realism.'; a Westmont College student per his bio); Gelsinger (Fox News op-ed, 2026-01-04: 'AI isn't just answering questions. It's shaping worldviews.'; executive chairman and head of technology at Gloo); Nieuwhof with Kenny Jahng (careynieuwhof.com, 2024-11-24: 'Embracing new methods always keeps the mission alive in ways that resisting them never will.'); Thacker (NAE, 2025-05-28: 'the value, dignity and exclusivity of humanity isn’t rooted in what we do but who we are as unique image bearers of our creator'); James (Crossway podcast, 2026-01-26: 'AI does not think. AI does not reason. AI does not contemplate. It is a machine.'); Watkin (TGC, 2026-08-24: 'AI can help us in many ways, and used wisely it could bring great benefits. But it cannot kneel.'); Pope Leo XIV (Vatican message, 2025-06-17: 'By definition, tools point to the human intelligence that crafted them...'; Catholic, labeled on the card only).
